result.title: Protective Perturbations Must Survive the Resize: Scale-Robust Image Immunization against Malicious Editing
result.summary: Protective perturbations aim to stop malicious instruction-guided editing of personal photos, but they are optimized and evaluated at the editor's working resolution, whereas shared photos have 10 megapixels or more and editors first downscale them by an unknown factor. We model this resize as a frequency-selective channel. In this model, a perturbation computed at the native resolution decays with the downscaling factor and is weak even without a resize, and a perturbation computed at a fixed working resolution protects only a window of scales. The best worst-case protection over an unknown range of scales degrades only logarithmically with the width of the range, and averaging over scales does not reach it. Guided by this analysis, we propose SRIM, which samples a grid of anchor scales covering the whole range, with weights that favor the currently weakest scale, at the cost of standard expectation over transformation. On full-resolution photos of 9 to 30 megapixels and downscaling factors from 2 to 8, SRIM raises the worst-case disruption of FLUX.2-klein edits from 0.192 LPIPS, attained by the strongest published protection, to 0.463. At equal visibility, it roughly doubles the protection. The same protected photos also protect against the 9B model and against FLUX.2-dev, with worst cases of 0.450 and 0.386 against at most 0.184 for published protections, and SRIM leads on InstructPix2Pix as well.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究图像保护性扰动在缩放信道下的衰减，提出 SRIM 通过多尺度锚点采样与偏向最弱尺度的加权，提升对指令引导式恶意编辑（如 FLUX.2）的防护鲁棒性。
AI.relevance_reason: 主题为对抗性图像防护以阻止图像编辑，不涉及 VLM 内部 latent 推理状态、证据筛选或停止决策；其多尺度频率信道分析或可作为相似度对尺度/分辨率敏感性的类比线索，但缺乏与本主线的实质联系。
